news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

An Army veteran unaware she was set to become a first-time grandma was mauled to death by a pack of dogs after being attacked in the yard of an abandoned home – as her grief-stricken pregnant daughter calls for justice.

Allison Lynn Anderson, 36, was found with “fatal injuries” on Nov. 16 after cops responded to reports of an unresponsive woman in a field in Cartersville, Georgia, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation revealed, citing preliminary autopsy results.

The circumstances behind the attack remain unclear but several of the dogs involved are now in the custody of Bartow County Animal Control, the GBI said, without revealing the exact number of animals involved in the attack.

Anderson, a mom of three who joined the Army in 2007, was set to become a grandmother – something which she wasn’t yet aware of, according to her 20-year-old daughter, Miley Garner, who is expecting her first child with her fiancé, Jesse Jarrett.

“If my mom knew that I was carrying her first grandchild, she would be over the moon and full of excitement,” Garner told WAFB.“I am so disgusted and absolutely heartbroken that the owners of these dogs did not have control over them. What my mom went through was torture.

“She deserves justice and even though what happened [on Nov. 16] was terrible, her heart is so pure she would forgive them.”

Tributes have been paid to Anderson – who has been described as someone with a “larger than life personality.”

“She was outgoing, full of personality, and never met a stranger. If someone needed help, Allison was there, whether she knew them or not,” her family said in an obit, announcing her unexpected passing.

“Allison lived life on her own terms. She danced to the beat of her own drum and wasn’t afraid to be exactly who she was.

“She loved being barefoot whenever she could and was happiest outdoors, especially near the water, whether she was swimming or fishing. Allison also loved music and singing, and those who heard her sing know she had a voice that was as beautiful as it was unforgettable.”

Neighbors have been left horrified by what unfolded in the yard, while others recalled how there was a large police presence in the aftermath amid the ongoing death probe.

“I had saw her about last week, I think it was. She had come by and I had talked to her. She was friends with my son and some of his friends. She was a real sweet girl — she was so sweet,” Betty Mathison, a neighbor, told Atlanta News First last Tuesday.

Investigators are combing through surveillance video from the area as part of their probe. No arrests have been made.
news.content:
در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را ببینید. یک کهنه‌سرباز ارتش که نمی‌دانست قرار است برای اولین بار مادربزرگ شود، پس از حمله در حیاط یک خانه متروکه توسط دسته‌ای سگ به طرز وحشیانه‌ای کشته شد – در حالی که دختر باردار و داغدارش خواستار اجرای عدالت است. جسد آلیسون لین اندرسون 36 ساله با «جراحات کشنده» در نوامبر پیدا شد. 16 پس از اینکه پلیس به گزارش‌های مربوط به یک زن بی‌هوش در مزرعه‌ای در کارترزویل، جورجیا پاسخ داد، اداره تحقیقات جورجیا با استناد به نتایج اولیه کالبدشکافی اعلام کرد. اداره تحقیقات جورجیا بدون اینکه تعداد دقیق حیوانات دخیل در حمله را اعلام کند، گفت که شرایط پشت این حمله هنوز مشخص نیست اما چندین سگ دخیل در این حادثه اکنون تحت کنترل اداره کنترل حیوانات شهرستان بارتو هستند. اندرسون، مادری سه فرزند که در سال 2007 به ارتش پیوست، قرار بود مادربزرگ شود - اتفاقی که هنوز از آن خبر نداشت، طبق گفته دختر 20 ساله‌اش، مایلی گارنر، که در انتظار اولین فرزندش با نامزدش، جسی جارت است.گارنر به WAFB گفت: «اگر مادرم می‌دانست که من نوه اولش را باردار هستم، از خوشحالی در پوست خود نمی‌گنجید و بسیار هیجان‌زده می‌شد.» «من از اینکه صاحبان این سگ‌ها کنترلی بر آنها نداشتند، بسیار منزجر و کاملاً دل‌شکسته هستم. آنچه مادرم تجربه کرد، شکنجه بود.«او سزاوار عدالت است و با وجود اینکه اتفاقی که [در 16 نوامبر] افتاد وحشتناک بود، قلب او آنقدر پاک است که آنها را می‌بخشد.»
به اندرسون - که او را فردی با «شخصیتی فراتر از حد معمول» توصیف کرده‌اند - ادای احترام شده است.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

New York’s City Council has gone mad, scrabbling from one bizarre or dangerous scheme to another, because its 51 members have lost their main power to serve their individual districts, their authority over land use.

Without the ability to protect residents from development plans, members turn to gambits that appeal to ideologues or special interests, whether it’s serving the Teamsters’ bid to hold up Amazon or animal-rights nuts’ crusade to spare lobsters from the pot or a double-whammy like banning horse carriages, which pleases elites and the developers who want the horse-stables property.

By design, the City Council is not a powerful body. It’s stuck largely following the mayor’s lead on the budget; it can’t impose or raise taxes; it must rely on the mayor to execute the laws it passes.

Even when the council has an oversight hearing, the mayor’s office can blow it off, as it did recently when members sought to investigate the pied-à-terre tax-rollout fiasco.

Each member used to have significant power over land use: For decades, the principle of “member deference” let members veto real-estate projects contrary to the interests of their district.

That forced developers to bargain with council members to gain valuable zoning variances by offering to fund neighborhood amenities like new schools or libraries, or by reducing a project’s scale to match the area’s character.

It also let members nix development their constituents despised.

Member deference was real democracy in action, often the only way that neighborhood residents could make their voices heard about community density and texture.

Yes, this caused problems, blocking developments of clear benefit to the wider city and prompting an alliance of central planners (especially subsidized-housing advocates) and real-estate interests to unite behind ballot proposals that stripped the City Council of most of its land-use-approval power to allow fast-tracking of projects in the name of “cutting red tape” and “efficiency.”

No longer able to stop even wildly unpopular development, members rush to find other ways to win popularity, please donors or just feel important.

Hence the flood of oddball initiatives — prohibiting the sale of pet birds; a city-run “payment fund” for gig workers; tweaks to food-delivery apps to make people tip more; preventing AI systems from making fun of elected officials.

Reformers have left the City Council without much useful to do — and idle hands do the devil’s work.
news.content: پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. شورای شهر نیویورک دیوانه شده است و از یک طرح عجیب یا خطرناک به طرحی دیگر می‌رود، زیرا 51 عضو آن قدرت اصلی خود را برای خدمت به مناطق فردی خود، یعنی اختیارشان بر کاربری زمین، از دست داده‌اند. اعضا بدون داشتن توانایی محافظت از ساکنان در برابر طرح‌های عمرانی، به شیوه‌هایی متوسل می‌شوند که برای ایدئولوگ‌ها یا گروه‌های ذی‌نفع خاص جذاب است، چه این که در خدمت تلاش اتحادیه رانندگان کامیون برای متوقف کردن آمازون باشد یا جنگ صلیبی دیوانگان حقوق حیوانات برای نجات خرچنگ‌ها از دیگ یا ضربه دوتایی مانند ممنوعیت کالسکه اسب، که مورد پسند نخبگان و سازندگان مسکنی است که می‌خواهند محل اصطبل‌های اسب را تصاحب کنند. شورای شهر ذاتاً نهادی قدرتمند نیست. این شورا عمدتاً در زمینه بودجه از رهبری شهردار پیروی می‌کند؛ نمی‌تواند مالیات وضع کند یا آن را افزایش دهد؛ برای اجرای قوانینی که تصویب می‌کند باید به شهردار متکی باشد. در خبرنامه روزانه Post Opinion ما مشترک شوید!لطفاً یک ایمیل معتبر وارد کنید. با کلیک کردن روی گزینه بالا، با شرایط استفاده و سیاست حفظ حریم خصوصی موافقت می‌کنید. حتی زمانی که شورا جلسه نظارتی برگزار می‌کند، دفتر شهردار می‌تواند آن را نادیده بگیرد، همانطور که اخیراً زمانی که اعضا خواستار بررسی شکست طرح مالیاتی pied-à-terre بودند، این کار را کرد. هر یک از اعضا زمانی قدرت قابل توجهی بر کاربری زمین داشتند: برای دهه‌ها، اصل «احترام به نظر اعضا» به اعضا اجازه می‌داد تا به پروژه‌های املاک و مستغلات که برخلاف منافع منطقه آنها بود، رأی منفی بدهند. این امر سازندگان را مجبور کرد تا با اعضای شورا چانه‌زنی کنند و با پیشنهاد تأمین مالی امکانات محله، مجوزهای تغییر کاربری ارزشمندی را کسب کنند.

news.originalContent:
One of Bangladesh’s best-known financial institutions has found itself at centre of political tensions amid protests and violence by supporters of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina.

Dhaka, Bangladesh – When attackers stormed a Grameen Bank branch in Kashiani last week, they did not just damage furniture and equipment. They also destroyed records accumulated over nearly three decades.

Solaiman Morol, the branch manager in Bangladesh’s Gopalganj district, said about a dozen men arrived on the afternoon of November 18 carrying machetes, petrol and tools to break the locks. Staff members were away on field visits.

The attackers looted the branch and tried to cut open its vault with a grinder. They took out about 40 sacks of vouchers and other documents and set them on fire. They also looted steel cupboards, filing cabinets, chairs, tables and other equipment. A staff member’s rice cooker was among the items taken away. “They said that after burning the records, nobody would have to repay their loans,” Morol said.

Videos of the attack later appeared online. Morol said he heard slogans including “Joy Bangla” and “Joy Bangabandhu”, associated with ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League, as well as calls to burn what the attackers described as “Yunus’s den”.

The branch has not been able to resume normal operations. Staff members have received threats and customers are worried about the safety of their deposits and loan records.

“A bank depends on trust. This is impacting our customers’ confidence. People who have deposits with us are becoming frightened,” Morol said.

It wasn’t a one-off incident.

The attack was part of a wider wave of violence against Grameen Bank. Its latest internal memorandum, dated November 23, records 97 attacks on branches and offices between November 10 and 23.

The attacks have put the Nobel Prize-winning institution founded by Muhammad Yunus at the centre of Bangladesh’s political tensions, months after he stepped down as chief adviser following Hasina’s removal from power in August 2024. Hasina supporters set fire to police stations and the homes of local MPs, and allegedly killed three BNP members in Faridpur and Narail.

Grameen Bank is one of Bangladesh’s best-known financial institutions. It pioneered a model of microcredit that provides small loans to people who often cannot access conventional banking services.

About 90 percent of its ownership belongs to its borrower-members, while the government holds the remaining 10 percent. It has around 10.6 million members, most of them rural women, according to its managing director, Sarder Akhter Hamed. Around 5.5 million borrowers have outstanding loans worth more than Tk19,000 crore ($1.53bn). Members also hold deposits of around Tk25,000 crore ($2bn) with the bank.

“There are many people in the communities we serve whom other banks and financial institutions are unwilling to lend to. We stand beside them and provide access to credit,” Hamed said.

The attacks have disrupted the bank’s work and left staff members worried about their safety. Hamed said the institution has around 21,000 employees and that the violence had affected them psychologically. “There is a sense of insecurity,” he said.

The government has blamed the Awami League, the party of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, for the attacks.

“The government is making every effort to maintain law and order,” Ziauddin Ahmed, additional secretary in charge of the political wing at the Ministry of Home Affairs, told Al Jazeera.

The attacks come amid renewed political activity by Hasina’s supporters, which has led to serious unrest in parts of the country, for example Gopalganj, her ancestral district. Hasina supporters have set fire to police stations and the homes of local MPs, and allegedly killed three BNP members.

Political analysts say Grameen Bank has become a symbol through which some Awami League supporters can direct their anger at Yunus, under whose interim rule Hasina’s party was banned from electoral politics. During Yunus’s stint as Bangladesh’s leader, Hasina was also convicted by a tribunal for massacres carried out against protesters who challenged her rule in 2024. Hasina faces a death sentence, but has recently asserted that she intends to return to Bangladesh from India, where she has lived in exile since she was ousted.

Mubashar Hasan, a researcher at the humanitarian and development research initiative at Western Sydney University, said the timing was significant.

“Her party has spent the week pushing for her return. Grameen Bank is the easiest symbol of Dr Yunus they can reach,” he said. “For the Awami League’s hardliners, Yunus is the face of their fall, so burning his bank is a way of hitting back at him.”

The attacks, Hasan argued, may also be intended to demonstrate that the party still has a presence on the streets, despite the ban. “Some of these attacks look like a performance of strength, especially in Gopalganj, to tell supporters ‘we are still here’,” he said.

Asif Mohammad Shahan, a professor in the department of development studies at the University of Dhaka, sees the violence as part of a broader political strategy.

He said the Awami League had two possible routes after the August 2024 uprising: acknowledge its mistakes and seek political rehabilitation, or try to force its way back into politics. In his assessment, the party has chosen the latter.

“The attack on Grameen Bank is actually an effort of sending a message of ‘politics of revenge’,” Shahan said.

He said the attacks could also be intended to provoke the government into a heavy-handed response, allowing the party to portray itself as a victim and challenge the government’s legitimacy.

The bank’s ownership structure makes the attacks especially consequential. Most of its shares belong to the poor women who depend on it for loans, savings and other financial services.

“When a branch burns, it’s their loan files, savings records and repayment schedules going up in smoke,” Hasan of Western Sydney University said.

He warned that disruption could push borrowers towards informal lenders and make it harder for them to continue their repayment cycles.

The damage is already affecting the bank’s operations. Hamed, the Grameen Bank managing director, said the institution had suspended the accrual of interest on outstanding loans at branches unable to operate because of the attacks.

The bank is also trying to protect its staff and property. Some branches have increased security and moved staff from locations considered particularly risky.

But the consequences extend beyond damaged buildings and lost records: At stake is also the confidence of customers in the bank.

The attacks have also raised questions about the ability of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s government to maintain law and order.

Ahmed, the Home Ministry official, said “it would be wrong to say that the government is struggling to contain the situation”. Police headquarters told Al Jazeera that eight cases had been filed and eight people arrested in connection with the attacks. “The problem is that our police force is somewhat short of manpower,” Ahmed said.

Shahan said the government’s response was being constrained by the knowledge that a tough crackdown could give the Awami League the chance to play victim. “The Awami League is baiting the government into attacking it so that it can quickly switch to playing the victim and try to delegitimise the government,” he said.

Hamed said police had responded whenever the bank sought help and in some cases had provided advance warnings about possible attacks. “For the most part, however, we have had to remain alert and protect ourselves,” he said.

“If the law-and-order situation in the country improves, confidence and trust [in the bank, too] will automatically return,” he said.

Talk about talking turkey.

Two feathered VIPs have checked into one of Washington’s most luxurious hotels, complete with plush beds, a red-carpet welcome and a crowd of eager photographers, ahead of President Trump’s annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon at the White House.

The presidential hopefuls arrived Sunday at the historic Willard InterContinental Washington, DC, where they were photographed strutting across a red carpet, posing for pictures and standing atop the hotel’s beds before their big day on the South Lawn.

The US Department of Agriculture celebrated their arrival on X, announcing a “SPECIAL DELIVERY TO WASHINGTON, DC!” and describing the birds as “two VERY special guests” receiving the presidential treatment.

Photographs shared by the USDA, credited to the White House and National Turkey Federation, showed the plump white birds making their grand entrance before an audience of hotel guests and photographers.

One turkey was even pictured riding through the hotel’s ornate hallways inside a travel crate perched on a brass luggage cart.

The pair appeared equally comfortable with the accommodations, with one bird spreading its feathers atop a neatly made bed while its companion stood nearby.

But before the turkeys meet the commander in chief, Americans have been invited to settle a pressing matter of national importance: What should they be called?

The White House launched an online contest offering three possible combinations: “Commander & Chief,” “Freedom & Feathers,” and “Honey & Ham.”

Voting on the names closed Sunday at 5 p.m. ET, with the winning pair expected to be announced before a second round of voting opens Monday at 8 a.m. That final vote will determine which turkey receives the official ceremonial pardon.

The birds, raised by American turkey farmers Scott and Becky Rightsell at Deans Gap Farm in West Virginia, have already received their own playful presidential biographies.

Both hatched July 15, but their tastes apparently differ. According to the White House, one enjoys Golden Delicious apples and scenic country drives, while the other prefers Dr Pepper and dreams of vacationing in Aggieland.

The pair was selected from a larger flock based on appearance and temperament, according to West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey’s office.

Their preparations included getting accustomed to crowds, camera lights and noise.

And for Americans who cannot get enough turkey-related excitement, the White House has unveiled “Gobble Getaway,” an online game challenging players to help a turkey dodge a chef armed with a net and roasting pan while making its way across the South Lawn to the pardon podium.

The annual Thanksgiving tradition dates back to 1947, when the National Turkey Federation first presented a holiday bird to President Harry Truman.

President John F. Kennedy spared a gift turkey in 1963, while President George H.W. Bush established the formal presidential turkey pardon in 1989.

Trump and first lady Melania Trump are scheduled to participate in this year’s ceremony on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 2 p.m. ET on the White House South Lawn.

Although the public gets to vote on which turkey receives the ceremonial pardon, both birds are traditionally spared the Thanksgiving dinner table.

For now, the pair can enjoy their luxury accommodations and newfound celebrity status, knowing their next stop is 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue rather than the oven.

news.originalContent:
Closed military zones in the occupied West Bank are being seized by settlers and made into staging posts for pogroms against Palestinians.

Ramallah, Occupied West Bank – Saleh Zahran had a room on his family’s land with a television, a fireplace, a fridge and solar panels. The kids would play in the groves, and the men stayed up late at night watching the stars.

“We’d cook, eat, drink, spend a whole day from morning to sunset,” he says.

Zahran, 39, inherited the farmland, with 120 olive trees, in Deir Abu Mishal, a village west of Ramallah, from his grandfather and father, splitting it among his brothers.

Between 70 and 80 percent of people in the village, which falls in Area B, under joint Israeli-Palestinian control, live off the land, and just a few years ago, there were no settlers nearby.

“We’d come and go whenever we wanted, pick our fruit at our own pace, sell, build, and marry off sons from the olives. Now, it’s all gone,” he told Al Jazeera.

Since settlers set up an outpost in Area B about 1km from his land in June, nobody in his family had been able to reach it. Settlers attacked their cars, and his elderly father was pepper-sprayed while trying to reach the farmland, he says.

On November 10, an Israeli High Court decision granted the village two days of army “coordinated” harvesting, something once unthinkable in Area B.

Zahran set out with his brothers to reach their lands for the first time in five months, but about 20 settlers came at them. They threw stones, smashed the family’s truck and his brother’s four-wheeler and slashed the tyres. He saw no soldiers, and police never arrived despite their calls.

The next day, the army and its liaison office were present. But farmers were held up until about 9am, shown a map of permitted areas, and told to leave by 2:30pm. Ghiyath Nasser, their lawyer, says villagers could reach less than a third of the area in question, so Zahran could harvest only about 20 of his 120 trees.

After five months, Zahran finally reached the farm room that day only to find settlers had stolen or smashed his belongings and were drawing water for their sheep from the two wells he had restored. The saplings he had planted last year had died of thirst.

On paper, it is the settlers who are barred from the Zahran family’s property and the land around Deir Abu Mishal. But in practice, it is Palestinian owners like Zahran who are kept out.

Nasser says that after his first legal petition, the army twice demolished the outpost – which was immediately rebuilt both times – then declared the site a closed military zone for Israelis only. That, Nasser argues, means soldiers cannot demand permits or “coordination” from Palestinian owners – their job is to keep settlers out.

“Sometimes they declare an area closed to settlers, but in the application they close it to Palestinians,” said Wail Qut, a lawyer with the Jerusalem Legal Aid and Human Rights Center (JLAC), who is from Madama, south of Nablus.

Kerem Navot and Peace Now’s July report found that, at the end of 2025, farm outposts effectively controlled more than 1 million dunams (247,105.4 acres), about 18 percent of the West Bank — roughly 750,000 dunams (185,329 acres) taken since late 2022.

In Madama, closures came first, and the outposts followed. Qut says its northern land was never declared a closed military zone, but the effect was the same.

About five years ago, the army gated the road from the village to Nablus, citing security concerns, he says. It was the only access to as much as a third of Madama’s land. The Israeli High Court dismissed the villagers’ petition after the army said farmers could reach the land on foot or by animal and apply for permits.

“It’s a de facto closure, though,” said Qut, with farmers still barred from entering.

Then, last April, an outpost of what Qut estimates are now 10 caravans appeared inside the closed area. He said the army suddenly reopened the gate for the settlers to use. Qut and his brother were stopped by a settler in the same area when they tried to pick olives there this year, forcing them to leave under armed threat.

Dror Etkes, founder of Kerem Navot, which tracks settler land takeovers, says such closures without orders are common across the occupied West Bank. “There is no vacuum in the West Bank,” he said. “Once an area is closed to Palestinian access, settlers sooner or later will come and take it over, and this is exactly what happened in Madama.”

But Qut finds the courts complicit too. When JLAC petitioned over the outpost north of Madama in September, the court gave the state until May 2027 to respond, rather than a few days, as Qut expected.

On November 13, a wedding was due to take place in al-Mughayyir, located at the northeastern edge of the Ramallah governorate. “Despite the pain and the suffering, people rejoice,” said Samir Abu Alia, 60, a village council member whose cousin’s son, Hassan Abu Alia, 30, was the groom. But soldiers violently cut the festivities short.

“The moment the patrols came down, they surrounded the hall, 20 army jeeps, and started throwing stun grenades between the men and the women,” recalled Abu Alia. Soldiers took the groom and relatives away from his bride for two hours. Abu Alia and others say the groom was beaten.

It began earlier that day on the eastern plain, when a settler grazing his flock inside a closed military zone claimed someone from al-Mughayyir had thrown firecrackers or shot at him, although he was unhurt. Soldiers accepted the settler’s claim at face value and then sealed and raided the village. The army quickly targeted the wedding, claiming there were gunshots and firecrackers, which attendees deny.

About 80 percent of al-Mughayyir’s 43,000 dunams (10,625.5 acres) lies beyond its eastern entrance, closed for years. Abu Alia says villagers can now move freely in only about 900 dunams (222.4 acres). “The rest of the land they’ve taken over, they stop people from reaching it, on the pretext of a military zone, on the pretext of security, on the pretext of I don’t know what.”

Here, the outpost came first. Village council member Marzouq Abu Naim says the first outpost on the eastern plain appeared in 2018 and has grown from 200 dunams to 5,000 dunams. He counts a dozen around the village. “One of the settlers comes, brings a tent, pitches it on a hilltop … the second day, the third day, you find there’s facilitation, something not normal: [authorities] run him water, they run him electricity, they lay a road to this tent,” he said.

According to Abu Naim, when villagers tried to use the eastern entrance about two months ago, settlers attacked and tried to burn cars and tractors, and the army did nothing to intervene.

Abu Naim, whose son, Jihad, 32, was shot dead by a settler during an invasion of the village school in April, also lost a 10-dunam grove of about 250 olive trees. “It wasn’t me who planted them, or my father — our grandfathers planted them.”

In August 2025, after a shooting wounded an Israeli teenager, the army ordered olive trees beside a settler road through the plain cleared as a “security threat”, and settlers joined in. Locals say more than 10,000 trees were eventually uprooted, including 230 belonging to Abu Alia.

Documents from the Israeli NGO Yesh Din show the area was closed for 30 days to “preserve the aims of the clearing”. Renewed in October 2025, the order extended to July 2026 with redrawn boundaries, and again through December.

The order bars everyone without a permit, settlers included. But Yesh Din’s legal objection says it is enforced only against the owners, while settlers graze, plough and build on their plots. When the army’s legal adviser declined to enforce the closure against settlers, he referred Yesh Din to the Israeli Defence Ministry’s legal adviser instead, which the NGO says was an effort to absolve the army of responsibility.

Lior Zur, a Yesh Din lawyer representing the petitioners, told Al Jazeera, “Through this policy of selective enforcement, the military turns closure orders into a mechanism for transferring possession of land from its lawful Palestinian owners to settler trespassers.”

The pattern runs across the West Bank. In March, a closed zone around Duma was enforced against Israeli solidarity activists protecting Bedouin families, rather than settlers; after soldiers removed the activists, settlers invaded the encampment, forcibly displacing the community the next day.

In Burin, farmland sits in closed zones renewed every month or two; settlers have gutted five greenhouses in these closed zones already. In Taybeh, an August order barred Israelis and foreigners, but settlers and outposts remained, including one near the edge of Area B that led to another unevenly enforced closed zone.

Similar cases have occurred in Ein al-Duyuk, Qusra, Umm al-Khair and elsewhere. In closed and firing zones the Israeli army has not used for decades, Etkes said, settlers are “filling in”, even though the orders formally apply to settlers, too.

The result, this olive harvest season, has been unprecedented levels of violence and access restrictions. The United Nations Humanitarian Country Team for the occupied Palestinian territory said on November 20 that more than 400 settler attacks that caused casualties or damage had been recorded since September, more than in any previous season. The infrequent “coordination” access windows, it said, are often followed by “cancellations, denial of entry, expulsion or attacks”.

“What started as local initiative has been adopted by the military and is today, maybe not a declared policy, but an implemented policy,” said Etkes. The outposts are “not legal, but they are completely supported by the military, by the government, without officialising it”. The Israeli Civil Administration has leased large areas of the West Bank to settlers for grazing, which they never do for Palestinians, Qut said.

“Military closed-zone orders and settler takeovers of Palestinian land are two complementary practices,” said Yair Dvir, spokesperson for Israeli NGO B’Tselem. “The military uses these orders to drive Palestinians off their land, while settlers are frequently allowed to remain or establish outposts.”

Back in Deir Abu Mishal, olives are rotting on trees as the season ends. Zahran’s three young children ask why they cannot return to the farm room for barbecues and the olive harvest. He tells them it is too dangerous. “Four or five settlers stop a whole village, 5,000-6,000 people, from going to the land,” Zahran said. “We are living the height of injustice.”
news.content: مناطق نظامی بسته در کرانه باختری اشغالی توسط شهرک نشینان تصرف شده و به ایستگاه هایی برای کشتار مردم فلسطین تبدیل می شود. رامالله، کرانه باختری اشغالی - صالح زهران در زمین خانواده اش اتاقی با تلویزیون، شومینه، یخچال و پنل های خورشیدی داشت. بچه‌ها در نخلستان‌ها بازی می‌کردند و مردها شب‌ها تا دیروقت بیدار می‌ماندند و ستاره‌ها را تماشا می‌کردند. او می‌گوید: «ما آشپزی می‌کردیم، می‌خوردیم، می‌نوشیدیم، یک روز کامل از صبح تا غروب آفتاب می‌گذراندیم. زهران، 39 ساله، زمین کشاورزی را با 120 درخت زیتون در دیر ابو مشال، روستایی در غرب رام الله، از پدربزرگ و پدرش به ارث برد و آن را بین برادرانش تقسیم کرد. بین 70 تا 80 درصد از مردم این روستا، که در منطقه B قرار دارد، تحت کنترل مشترک اسرائیل و فلسطینیان بودند، چند سال پیش در آنجا ساکنان این سرزمین نبودند. در نزدیکی او به الجزیره گفت: «ما هر زمان که می‌خواستیم می‌آمدیم و می‌رفتیم، میوه‌هایمان را با سرعت خودمان می‌چینیم، می‌فروشیم، می‌سازیم و پسران زیتون را به عقد خود در می‌آوریم. حالا همه چیز از بین رفته است.» از آنجایی که شهرک‌نشینان در ماه ژوئن یک پاسگاه در منطقه B در حدود 1 کیلومتری زمین او ایجاد کردند، هیچ‌کس از خانواده‌اش نتوانست به آن برسد. او می گوید که شهرک نشینان به ماشین های آنها حمله کردند و پدر سالخورده اش در حالی که سعی می کرد به زمین های کشاورزی برسد مورد اسپری فلفل قرار گرفت. در 10 نوامبر، یک تصمیم دادگاه عالی اسرائیل دو روز برداشت «هماهنگ» ارتش را به این روستا داد، چیزی که زمانی غیرقابل تصور بود که در منطقه ب.زهران به همراه برادرانش برای اولین بار در پنج ماه گذشته به سرزمین‌هایشان برسند، اما حدود 20 شهرک نشین به آنها آمدند. خیابان انداختند

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino pushed a plan to sell off a slice of the World Cup for up to 96 years in a $20 billion Wall Street deal — and FIFA’s own finance chief was kept in the dark until the day bosses voted on it, leaked files show.

The no-bid push — backed by Josh Kushner’s Thrive Capital — drew in some of Wall Street’s biggest names.

Jamie Dimon’s JPMorgan advised FIFA and helped set the $20 billion price, the papers show.

JPMorgan asset management chief Mary Erdoes — once touted as a possible next CEO — met privately with Infantino after Patriots owner Robert Kraft put them in touch, they said, and the Park Avenue giant later landed the valuation gig. A JPMorgan spokesperson declined to comment.

In a leaked email seen by The Post, FIFA CFO Thomas Peyer also warned an outside buyer would likely seek a “short-term improvement of financials to “dress the bride,” a Wall Street term that means making a firm look attractive to potential suitors.

That could hurt the product long term and “significantly deprioritize free-to-air to the benefit of pay-wall,” he wrote before deciding to abstain in the vote.

Peyer wrote he was only briefed July 18 — the eve of the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey — and had “not received the underlying calculations on the valuation.”

The Post has sought comment from FIFA and Thrive Capital.

Less than an hour later, Infantino’s chief of staff, Daniel O’Toole, backed his own pitch.

“For the avoidance of doubt, I hereby provide my approval,” he wrote. The plan won early management approval anyway, emails and insiders said.

Internal FIFA files obtained by The Post show there was no open bidding. FIFA’s finance team was “not directly privy to the construction of this transaction,” an internal sign-off form states.

The plan would have pumped up to $4.22 billion in outside cash into a new US firm — FIFA Forward Enterprises, or FFE — to run FIFA’s commercial rights.

FIFA would have kept a majority stake, yet private buyers still would have won veto power over big business moves, the files show.

The lock-in would have stretched nearly a century. FIFA would have been on the hook to renew the deal in 12-year blocks for up to 96 years. Only a major, unfixed breach by FFE could break it.

The July 17 term sheet made FIFA’s sitting president — currently Infantino — chair of FFE’s board, with a tie-breaking vote.

The plan also sought to waive directors’ fiduciary duties to the new firm to the full extent allowed by law.

It explicitly let directors vote for the party that picked them, subject to conflict rules to be set later for licensing deals.

Up to 5% of FFE’s stock was set aside for a bonus pool for the new firm’s management. In theory, it could have paid out up to $50 million for each $1 billion in value above $20 billion.

FIFA’s memo said the pool aimed to “ensure sufficient motivation to perform well.

The memo leaves names blank, and any payout needed board and buyer sign-off, a pay study, and continued service. The files reviewed by The Post did not show the names of who would run the new entity.

Thrive’s July 17 “backstop” letter gave Kushner’s firm sweeping perks. Thrive pledged to buy shares other buyers passed on. It also locked in at least 60% of outside shares sold and won waivers from ownership caps set for other buyers.

If signed, the letter could also have barred FIFA from talks with rival lead buyers until the deal closed or until July 17, 2027 — whichever came first. That bar would have stood even if FIFA’s member nations or Council voted no.

Thrive stood to win a steep break fee if FIFA broke that promise.

If FIFA cut a rival deal during that window, FIFA — or the rival buyers — would have owed Thrive free stock equal to 1.25% of the new firm, or an equal stake in any rival vehicle. At the proposed price, that stake was worth roughly $250 million.

The copy obtained by The Post leaves FIFA’s signature line blank.

It is unclear whether the backstop letter was ever signed or formally ended. FIFA’s memo stressed that if the letter took effect, FIFA did not have to close the spin-off deal — but could not pursue a similar deal with another buyer for a year.

The memo says there was no tender “owing to the specific and unique nature of the proposed investment.”

FIFA spoke with Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners, Greg Maffei’s BANN Ventures and Avenue Capital, it says. Those firms either passed on the terms or lacked the required cash. The memo does not say which applied to which firm.

The plan also left the door open to foreign sovereign wealth funds from precleared countries, though none are named as buyers.

FIFA maintained the venture would bring in fresh cash for soccer growth while keeping its authority over sporting decisions.

Months of private Wall Street talks led up to the vote, insiders said, that involved JPMorgan‘s Erdoes, ex-Liberty Media boss Greg Maffei and Thrive.

Infantino went to Jared Kushner’s office on Nov. 4, 2025, and Jan. 14, 2026, insiders said. It is unclear whether President Trump’s son-in-law was there on those occasions.

Infantino was on a video call with Josh Kushner, whose firm became the deal’s anchor, and Maffei as early as Dec. 8, 2025 — seven months before FIFA’s finance chief says he was briefed — according to a timeline reviewed by The Post.

Infantino held at least six additional discussions with Josh Kushner regarding FFE, and at least four discussions with Jared Kushner in the months before Josh Kushner’s Thrive Capital investment firm, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Thrive Capital spokesman Christian Seiersen refused to answer questions about the talks when initially contacted by The Post on Wednesday.

“The level of speculation in here is frankly crazy, and we are not planning to dignify (sic) with a response,” he said.

Greg Maffei did not reply to an emailed request for comment.

Infantino, 56, pulled the plug on the deal July 31 amid a global backlash from soccer groups and fans.

The news could add to the heat on the Swiss-Italian boss. The Post earlier revealed how his inner circle worked Trump team contacts to land a rare humanitarian visa for his Nicaraguan housemaid. The Post also broke how his family and dogs snagged VIP diplomatic perks at Miami’s airport.

FIFA pushed back on both reports. It said it checks staff immigration status, Infantino pays for his home staff himself, and his family had the right to ask for free airport VIP services.

Top Infantino aide Carlos Cordeiro quit in protest on July 31 at the sell-off plan and accused FIFA of “mortgaging football’s future without any compelling justification.”

The former Goldman Sachs partner was neither told about nor consulted on the deal as it took shape, two sources said. “I had no involvement in this proposal,” Cordeiro said in his resignation statement.

The leaked paperwork says the shares were priced at $20 billion, down from about $50 billion for the whole business.

That’s because the new firm would first have to pay FIFA’s running costs, guaranteed cash for its members, and other development money. FIFA had negotiated the price up from $15 billion, it adds.

Compare that $20 billion price tag with FIFA’s own books: a record $14 billion in budgeted revenue for 2027–2030 alone, including $6.1 billion from TV rights. That’s up from a budgeted $13 billion for the four years capped by this summer’s World Cup.

“There was no rationale, and there’s no way you could have convinced anybody that FIFA needed to do what they did on pure economic terms. To me, it sounds low. This is all of FIFA Inc. This is all of the commercial activity: ticketing, hospitality, sponsorship, broadcasting,” said one senior FIFA insider.

At $20 billion, the proposed equity price tag for world soccer’s biggest cash cow was just $3 billion more than Forbes’ $17 billion valuation for the Dallas Cowboys — a single NFL team that hasn’t won a Super Bowl in 30 years — and barely more than two New York Yankees franchises.

FIFA’s former chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, also left the organization in mid-August, saying staff had been “deceived” by Infantino and called the deal a “project of one person.”

Europe’s soccer bosses at UEFA have gone to US courts seeking proof for a possible Swiss criminal complaint. The targets: Infantino and potentially other FIFA officials, over alleged mismanagement.

Even members of FIFA’s ruling Council, the presidents of national soccer federations, will only get tight access to key files on the scrapped plan in Zurich, under secrecy rules earlier reported by The Post.

FIFA has called UEFA’s court filings a “smear campaign.” On Nov. 12, a Manhattan federal judge shut out two FIFA US arms that tried to join UEFA’s cases seeking files from Thrive, Josh Kushner, JPMorgan and Erdoes. The ruling did not decide UEFA’s underlying requests.

Infantino’s allies point to his spending on grassroots soccer. FIFA offers each of its 211 member nations up to $8 million in the current four-year cycle.

FIFA says its Forward plan has funded nearly 600 new pitches and over 200 local leagues in his first two terms, reaching more than 300,000 players.

Supporters also credit him with growing the men’s World Cup to 48 teams and the women’s event to 32 — with 48 set for 2031. They say that gives smaller nations a shot at soccer’s biggest stages.

Still, critics say the failed deal could define his reign.

“Forget about the grandeur and the success of the [2026] World Cup,” a senior FIFA source said. “Now it’s lost. This is what people will remember.”
news.content:
در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را ببینید. طبق اسناد فاش‌شده، رئیس فیفا، جیانی اینفانتینو، طرحی را برای فروش بخشی از جام جهانی به مدت حداکثر 96 سال در یک معامله 20 میلیارد دلاری در وال‌استریت پیش برد — و رئیس امور مالی خود فیفا تا روزی که مدیران به آن رأی دادند، از موضوع بی‌اطلاع بود. این طرح بدون مناقصه — که توسط Thrive Capital متعلق به جاش کوشنر حمایت می‌شد — برخی از بزرگترین نام‌های وال‌استریت را جذب کرد. طبق اسناد، JPMorgan جِیمی دیمون به فیفا مشاوره داد و به تعیین قیمت 20 میلیارد دلاری کمک کرد. آنها گفتند که مری اردوس، مدیر بخش مدیریت دارایی JPMorgan — که زمانی به عنوان مدیرعامل بعدی احتمالی مطرح شده بود — پس از اینکه رابرت کرافت، مالک پاتریوتس، آنها را با هم آشنا کرد، به صورت خصوصی با اینفانتینو ملاقات کرد و غول ساکن پارک اِوِنِو بعداً قرارداد ارزیابی را به دست آورد. سخنگوی جی‌پی‌مورگان از اظهارنظر در این مورد خودداری کرد. در یک ایمیل افشا شده که The Post آن را مشاهده کرده است، توماس پایر، مدیر مالی فیفا، همچنین هشدار داد که یک خریدار خارجی احتمالاً به دنبال «بهبود کوتاه‌مدت وضعیت مالی» برای «آراستن عروس» خواهد بود، اصطلاحی در وال‌استریت که به معنای جذاب کردن یک شرکت برای خریداران بالقوه است. او قبل از تصمیم‌گیری برای رأی ممتنع نوشت که این کار می‌تواند در بلندمدت به این محصول آسیب برساند و «اولویت پخش رایگان را به نفع پخش پولی به طور قابل‌توجهی کاهش دهد». پایر نوشت که تنها در 18 ژوئیه - یک روز قبل از فینال جام جهانی بین اسپانیا و آرژانتین در ورزشگاه مت‌لایف در نیوجرسی - به او اطلاعاتی داده شده بود و «محاسبات اصلی مربوط به ارزیابی را دریافت نکرده بود.»
واشنگتن پست از فیفا و Thrive Capital درخواست کرده است که نظر خود را اعلام کنند. کمتر از یک ساعت بعد، رئیس دفتر اینفانتینو، دا

news.originalContent:
At least 15 people are killed in multiple attacks, days after Russian President Putin promises a ‘painful’ response to Ukrainian attacks.

Rescuers in Ukraine have raced to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partially collapsed in a Russian strike after attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people.

Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly drone and missile barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter while the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year.

An overnight strike on Dymer, about 45km (30 miles) north of the Ukrainian capital, hit a five-storey building, killing at least 11 people, Kyiv regional official Tymur Tkachenko said on Monday.

“Rescuers recovered the body of another person from beneath the rubble,” Tkachenko wrote on Telegram, confirming the death toll had risen to 11.

Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said earlier on Telegram that the dead included a teenager.

It said rescuers were searching for 11 people, including two children, who were “not responding or cannot be reached”.

Rescuers had managed to pull out survivors from the rubble, including a 79-year-old woman and a child, Tkachenko said.

Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine, reporting from Kyiv, said people were believed to still be under the rubble.

“Rescuers are still at the site, working to try to pull people out from under the rubble dead or alive,” she said.

A Russian strike on a supermarket killed three other people and wounded 15, including three children, in Vyshneve, a city just south of Kyiv, Mayor Illya Dikov wrote on Facebook.

“People had simply gone to the store to buy groceries. An ordinary shopping trip turned into a tragedy due to a Russian attack,” Tkachenko said.

A strike on a private home in nearby Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.

Russia also struck a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said on social media.

Moscow has ramped up attacks on Ukraine and its energy network in particular as temperatures drop to around freezing.

Putin promised on Thursday that Russia would respond to Ukrainian attacks on the Kerch Bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule over Ukraine’s Russian-annexed Crimean Peninsula, with “much more painful” attacks.

Ukraine hit the bridge three times in a week, severing the part of it used by vehicles and halting train services.

Meanwhile, drones attacked oil storage facilities in Russia’s Tatarstan region, damaging several, but there were no immediate reports of deaths or injuries, according to the Interfax news agency, which quoted local authorities.

“A fire broke out there,” Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova reported from Moscow, adding that the attack targeted the facility in Tatarstan’s Almetyevsk area.

Shapovalova said drone attacks were also reported in the Novoshakhtinsk area in Rostov, hitting a petroleum products plant and causing a fire in a storage tank.

She added that an attack was also reported in the city of Perm in the Volga region, where a large oil refinery is located.

Our correspondents said the attacks in Tatarstan, which is about 1,000km (620 miles) away from the Ukrainian border, demonstrate Kyiv’s ability to penetrate deep inside Russia.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukraine’s forces sank the Russian corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest ships, commissioned in 2023, near the coast of Libya using seven Ukrainian-made naval drones.

Zelenskyy said they hit a second target, the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara. The Ukrainian president said it was used by Russia to transport weapons.

“We continue operations in designated waters,” he said on Telegram.

Zelenskyy added that a Russian Ka-27 combat helicopter was destroyed along with the corvette.
news.content: چند روز پس از آن که پوتین رئیس جمهور روسیه وعده پاسخ "دردناک" به حملات اوکراین را داد، حداقل 15 نفر در حملات متعدد کشته شدند. امدادگران در اوکراین برای یافتن ساکنان محبوس شده زیر آوار یک بلوک آپارتمانی که در حمله روسیه پس از حملات به منطقه کیف دست کم 15 کشته برجای گذاشت، تلاش کردند. مسکو با پهپادها و رگبارهای موشکی شبانه اوکراین را در حالی که این کشور جنگ زده برای زمستانی دیگر آماده می شود در حالی که تهاجم تمام عیار پنجمین سال خود را سپری می کند، اوکراین را در هم می کوبد. به گزارش روز دوشنبه Tymurkaal منطقه Tymurkaal یک مقام رسمی اعلام کرد که حمله شبانه به دایمر، در حدود 45 کیلومتری (30 مایلی) شمال پایتخت اوکراین، به ساختمانی 5 طبقه اصابت کرد و حداقل 11 نفر کشته شدند. تکاچنکو در تلگرام نوشت: «امدادگران جسد یک فرد دیگر را از زیر آوار بیرون آوردند.» سرویس اورژانس دولتی اوکراین پیشتر در تلگرام اعلام کرد که کشته شدگان شامل یک نوجوان نیز می شود. این سازمان اعلام کرد که امدادگران در جستجوی 11 نفر از جمله دو کودک هستند که «به آنها پاسخ داده نمی شود». تکاچنکو گفت که امدادگران موفق شده اند بازماندگان را از زیر آوار بیرون بکشند، از جمله یک زن 79 ساله و یک کودک. آدری مک آلپاین، خبرنگار الجزیره، که از کیف گزارش می دهد، گفت: گمان می رود افراد هنوز زیر آوار هستند. او گفت: "امدادگران هنوز در محل هستند و تلاش می کنند تا افراد را از زیر آوار بیرون بکشند." و مجروح

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Jensen Huang’s lover was in direct contact with China’s spy agency while she was having an affair with the now-former Nvidia chief, a bombshell report claims.

Alice Huang – no relation to the founder of the AI company – is believed to have been recruited by Beijing’s Ministry of State Security (MSS), according to US intelligence, and she was in contact with an agent between spring 2025 and this fall, the New York Times reported, citing sources familiar with the intelligence assessments.

The period overlaps her affair with billionaire Huang – who quit his role as the chipmaking giant’s CEO on Nov. 12 after the company was engulfed in turmoil amid the revelations of his extramarital affairs with not only Alice Huang but also an exec who reported to him.

It’s unclear, however, if Alice Huang passed on any insider information to the agent while having her tryst with Jensen Huang. Neither the White House nor the State Department has commented on the allegations.

However, President Trump was warned about Alice Huang’s alleged links to Beijing in June 2025 – which would’ve been just months after the first contact between the honeypot and official was established.

The Times report also claims US intelligence agencies have uncovered evidence that suggests that Alice Huang’s business partner and husband, Kang Wei, worked with the MSS, heightening suspicions that Jensen Huang was the target of an intelligence operation.

Kang Wei, who ran an extensive Beijing-backed AI data center empire in China and secured investments worth more than $9 billion from 2021 to 2024 as part of a government-backed push to build out AI infrastructure in China, has told people he introduced his wife to Jensen Huang.

Authorities continue to investigate Alice Huang and Kang Wei’s role in a network of companies which have been accused of smuggling Nvidia-made AI chips to China, violating US export controls.

Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center firm accused of export control violations, strongly denies any wrongdoing, previously claiming that the allegations are “not supported by verifiable evidence.”

Shipping logs have been recovered as evidence that links Alice Huang and Kang Wei to the network of companies under investigation, according to the Times report.

China has strongly denied claims Alice Huang was committing corporate espionage.

Beijing’s foreign ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, previously branded the allegation “unsubstantiated.”

“It is nothing but smears against China,” he said.

Meanwhile, Colette Kress is serving as Nvidia’s interim CEO following Huang’s dramatic resignation, but President Trump has reiterated his support for the tycoon.

“I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post Sunday night. “It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.”

The latest show of support came just two days after Trump said he’d love Huang to “be given a second chance.”

“You know, we’re a country of second chances,” Trump told reporters in Washington Friday.

“And he put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies.”

“And, I think the company [Nvidia], if they were smart, they’d take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work.”

Trump has always denied knowledge of Alice Huang being a Chinese spy.
news.content: پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. یک گزارش بمب ادعا می کند که معشوقه جنسن هوانگ مستقیماً با آژانس جاسوسی چین در تماس بوده است. نیویورک تایمز گزارش داد که نیویورک تایمز به نقل از منابع آگاه با ارزیابی های اطلاعاتی گزارش داد که آلیس هوانگ - که هیچ ارتباطی با موسس شرکت هوش مصنوعی ندارد - طبق اطلاعات اطلاعاتی ایالات متحده، گمان می رود که توسط وزارت امنیت دولتی پکن (MSS) استخدام شده باشد و او بین بهار 2025 تا پاییز امسال با یک مامور در تماس بوده است. مدیرعامل در نوامبر 12 پس از آن که شرکت در میان افشای روابط خارج از ازدواج او نه تنها با آلیس هوانگ، بلکه همچنین یکی از مدیران اجرایی که به او گزارش داده بود، غرق در آشفتگی شد. با این حال، مشخص نیست که آیا آلیس هوانگ در حین تلاش با جنسن هوانگ، هر گونه اطلاعات داخلی را به مامور انتقال داده است یا خیر. نه کاخ سفید و نه وزارت امور خارجه در مورد این اتهامات اظهار نظری نکرده اند. با این حال، رئیس جمهور ترامپ در مورد ارتباط ادعایی آلیس هوانگ با پکن در ژوئن 2025 هشدار داده شد - که تنها چند ماه پس از برقراری اولین تماس بین هانی پات و مقام رسمی بود. گزارش تایمز همچنین ادعا می‌کند که آژانس‌های اطلاعاتی ایالات متحده شواهدی را کشف کرده‌اند که نشان می‌دهد، شریک تجاری و همسر آلیس هوانگ، کانگ وی، با MSS کار می‌کرده است و این ظن را تشدید می‌کند که جنسن هوانگ هدف یک عملیات اطلاعاتی بوده است. news.originalContent:
A new report by UK-based charity Oxfam shows how Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland’.

More than three years of Israel’s genocidal war has turned Gaza into “a toxic wasteland”, with poisoned water and contaminated soil threatening the survival of Palestinians in the enclave of 2.3 million people.

Israel’s use of explosives and incendiary weapons has caused environmental contamination across more than 99 percent of Gaza, according to a new report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS).

“Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza includes military assaults on its environment, which are environmental war crimes threatening life now and for generations to come,” said Amitabh Behar, Oxfam’s international executive director.

“The destruction and contamination of Gaza will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival. This would breach Israel’s legal obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law,” he said in a statement.

“Palestinians living in Gaza are being exposed to toxins in multiple ways through air, food, water and via direct contact with contaminated soils and debris.”

The report shows how Israel’s destruction of buildings and the environment has contaminated the air, soil, food and water in the enclave.

It also emphasises the urgent need for a full independent investigation to identify and reduce the risks to Palestinian lives.

Pollutants from bombardment, fires, rubble and untreated sewage can reach Palestinians through the air they breathe, the water they drink and the food they eat.

Oxfam’s report, which uses satellite imagery, remote sensing, scientific analysis and other open-source data, gives a comprehensive picture to date of the impact of the Israeli assault on Gaza, which has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians. More than 1,500 Palestinians have been killed since the so-called “ceasefire” was signed in October 2025.

In September 2025, a UN international commission of inquiry said Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. And the International Court of Justice is hearing a case of genocide against Israel. In January, the ICJ said it was plausible that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

The report came a day after world leaders failed to reach a consensus on climate change at the 31st Climate Change Conference (COP31) of the United Nations.

Explosions, fires and the destruction of buildings and infrastructure release pollutants that settle on rubble and soil.

Wind, traffic and debris clearance send them back into the air. Oxfam’s analysis points to the highest concentrations in Gaza City, Jabalia and the North Gaza governorate.

Israel’s continuous bombardment has also generated substantial greenhouse gas emissions, with further emissions expected from clearing debris and rebuilding.

A study cited in the report estimated direct conflict emissions at more than 1.3 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) by January 2025.

By October 11, 2025, Israeli ground operations directly affected about 283sq km (109sq miles) of Gaza’s 365sq km (141sq miles), or 78 percent of the area, Oxfam estimates.

The UN Environment Programme estimates that the assault since October 7, 2023, generated 61 million tonnes of debris, which is about 29 tonnes of rubble per person living in Gaza now. More than 90 percent of Palestinians have been forcibly displaced, most of them multiple times.

Oxfam estimates that the mountains of rubble would require 2.1 million dump truckloads to clear them, equivalent to 736 trips around the circumference of the entire planet.

The amount of rubble that needs to be cleared is about eight times the 7.65 million tonnes estimated in Iraq’s Mosul during the 2017 conflict.

The report identifies at least one potential contamination source across more than 99 percent of Gaza. Gaza City, Khan Younis, Rafah, Jabalia and the Salah al-Din Street corridor showed the greatest overlap of potential hazards.

Unexploded munitions can leach contaminants into soil and groundwater as their casings corrode. Damaged vehicles, batteries and fuel stores add to the risks along military routes and former positions.

A study cited by Oxfam estimated emissions across the wider conflict cycle at 33.2 million tonnes of CO2e, including an estimate of 31.4 million tonnes of carbon emissions that will occur from reconstruction.

According to a report by Palestinian Water Authority cited by Oxfam, Gaza’s daily water supply fell from 334,107 cubic metres before October 2023 to 54,747 cubic metres in June 2024, a drop of about 84 percent. By April 2026, emergency repairs had brought it back to 130,315 cubic metres a day, still 61 percent below pre-assault levels.

Nine of 61 reservoirs were operational, with combined storage sufficient to provide 18 litres per person for one day.

Gaza’s Coastal Aquifer historically supplied 81 percent of the territory’s water. Oxfam says 97 percent of the aquifer was already chemically polluted before October 2023.

Decades of overpumping amid Israel’s air, land and sea blockade of Gaza allowed seawater to seep in. Untreated sewage, farm runoff and waste disposal added to the pollution.

In July 2026, Gaza’s Ministry of Health detected faecal coliforms in 15 of 79 groundwater wells (19 percent) tested. Oxfam identified North Gaza, Gaza City and Deir el-Balah as the areas most at risk from contaminated drinking water. An assessment in 2021 reported faecal coliforms in 2 percent of wells.

July tests found that 61 of 79 wells (77.2 percent) had total dissolved solids above 1,000 milligrams per litre, 400mg above the level at which the World Health Organization says water becomes increasingly unpleasant to drink.

By April 2024, Israel’s assault had destroyed all six of Gaza’s wastewater treatment plants. An estimated 40,000 cubic metres of raw sewage enter the Mediterranean daily, enough to fill 16 Olympic-size pools.

By April 2026, 19 percent of pumping stations and about 30 percent of the sewer network still functioned at least partly.

Gaza’s waste collection fleet fell from 261 vehicles to 48.

Both main landfills remained inaccessible. Of at least 56 temporary dumps, only 11 were accessible and operating.

These sites generally lack barriers to protect soil and groundwater. By April 2026, an estimated 1.45 million people lived in areas affected by rodents and other pests.

Before October 2023, Gaza’s farms supplied about 95 percent of the fresh vegetables people ate. By late 2025, more than 87 percent of cropland was damaged.

Oxfam says only 3 percent was accessible and undamaged.

By October 2024, the UN had reported that more than one million olive trees had been uprooted.

Oxfam identified more than 7,200 damaged greenhouses and documented the destruction of facilities that preserved and distributed Palestinian seeds.

Before the assault, Gaza’s fisheries produced about 4,660 tonnes of fish a year, with fish farms adding 750 tonnes.

In July 2026, an estimated 1.2 million people (59 percent) faced crisis levels of acute food shortages or worse, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, cited by the report.

The report also records the loss of roughly 95 percent of cattle and a collapse in fishing.

The average daily catch from October 2023 to April 2024 was 7.3 percent of its 2022 level. Oxfam warns that contaminants could enter crops and seafood as production resumes.

Gaza’s gross domestic product fell by 83 percent in 2024 to $362m, the report says.

Damage to farms, workshops and factories has stripped people of income and the means to resume work. Debris removal, repairs and farming could expose workers to asbestos, silica and other hazards for years.

Among the commerce and industry establishments assessed, 92 percent sustained damage, including 72 percent that were destroyed.

A joint World Bank, European Union and UN assessment, cited by Oxfam, put direct physical damage at $35.2bn and economic losses at $22.7bn by October 2025.

It estimated recovery and reconstruction needs at $71.4bn over a decade, including $26.3bn in the first 18 months.

Disease prevalence in Gaza recorded more than 1.9 million cases of acute respiratory infection and about 81,000 cases of acute watery diarrhoea in January and February 2026. More than 36,000 of the diarrhoea cases were among children aged below five years. Gaza recorded more than 496,000 cases of acute watery diarrhoea in 2025.

In 2024, vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 was detected in Gaza’s wastewater. A child was later diagnosed with paralytic polio, Gaza’s first reported case in 25 years. The report also cites the detection of multidrug-resistant pseudomonas in water at primary healthcare centres.

Oxfam says the destruction of Gaza’s water, food and sanitation systems may be relevant to alleged crimes under the Rome Statute and to assessing whether Israel violated the Genocide Convention.

A genocide finding requires proof of intent to destroy a protected group, in whole or in part. Oxfam calls for full reparations where violations are established.

Its five-stage plan calls for securing access and reducing exposure, testing for contamination, screening sites and making essential repairs, treating contaminated sites and managing hazardous waste, then rebuilding with safeguards and long-term monitoring.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said his country was behind an attack on a Russian warship off Libya on Sunday, claiming Ukrainian naval drones sank the vessel.

Zelensky said Monday in a post on X that Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made naval drones in the operation, which sank a Russian corvette.

The Ukrainian leader described the ship as one of Russia’s newest vessels commissioned in 2023 during the invasion.

“We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia’s aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons,” he said.

Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelensky said Moscow used to transport weapons. He added that a Ka-27 military helicopter was destroyed in the attack.

Zelensky thanked the Security Service of Ukraine, known as the SBU, and other Ukrainian defense forces that took part in what he described as “an exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war.”

Zelensky said he received detailed briefings on Sunday and Monday and that “the targets we set were achieved.”

The strike by sea drones severely damaged the Russian navy corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya, according to two Libyan officials.

Residents in Benghazi heard loud explosions and saw fire at the base early Sunday. Civil defense rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said.

The vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies as part of a cooperation agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, the statement said without providing details about the vessel or its cargo.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from a concert by American rapper Don Toliver after an unknown substance was released in the crowd, British police said Monday.

Greater Manchester Police said officers were called around 10 p.m. Sunday to the Co-op Live arena after reports of people being affected by a substance, initially believed to be tear gas. Footage shared on social media appeared to show concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths as they left the venue.

The force declared a “major incident,” which allows different emergency services to coordinate their response.

Concertgoer Ben Stevenson told the Manchester Evening News said he was in the standing area of the arena when he “started coughing and (my) eyes were kind of itchy.”

He said Toliver left the stage and the venue lights came on, but it was not until almost an hour later that an announcement was made saying “due to a unforeseen issue the show is over and please make your way out at your own pace.”

One person was taken to a hospital and more than 50 were assessed at the scene, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms, the North West Ambulance Service said.

It said “decontamination is being carried out as a precaution” at the venue.

Police Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said “anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital.”

“We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about,” she said.

Co-op Live, which opened in 2024, is about 2 miles (3.2 kilometers) from Manchester Arena, where 22 people were killed when a bomber blew himself up during an Ariana Grande concert in 2017.

Co-op Live said in a statement that venue bosses were working with police to identify the cause of the incident.Grammy Award- nominated trap and R&B rapper-singer Toliver, who features on the soundtrack to the new “Grand Theft Auto” game, is scheduled to perform at London’s O2 Arena on Monday and OVO Arena Wembley on Tuesday as part of his Nitrous tour.

news.originalContent:
Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang says humankind’s actions over next year will have ‘great consequence’ for the world.

Meta’s top AI executive has sounded the alarm about the risk of humanity losing control of AI, warning that superintelligence that far exceeds the human intellect is imminent.

Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang issued the warning on Sunday after an employee at AI giant Anthropic announced that he had used Claude to solve the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most difficult problems in mathematics.

Wang said the breakthrough dwarfed any human achievement for “sheer intellectual might”.

The 29-year-old executive said the milestone showed that emerging AI models will be “clearly superhuman” at improving themselves, as well as “massively accelerating” research in fields such as biology, armaments and economics.

“Superintelligence is arriving,” Wang said on X.

“How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in.”

Wang, who co-founded Scale AI before joining Meta as the tech giant’s first chief AI officer last year, said it is unlikely humankind will be able to control AI that achieves unconstrained recursive self-improvement or is “1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field.”

“Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully,” Wang said.

AI safety advocates have identified recursive self-improvement – where AI models become capable of advancing without human input – as a critical tipping point after which humanity could lose the ability to control the technology.

While the risks of frontier AI have stoked intense debate in Silicon Valley, there is no consensus on how to maximise the benefits of the technology without exposing humanity to catastrophic risks.

Meta has largely positioned itself on the more optimistic side of the debate, with CEO and cofounder Mark Zuckerberg rejecting calls by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for a coordinated slowdown in development to beef up guardrails.

In an essay published in August, Zuckerberg lamented that discussions about AI were “filled with doom” and said the technology should lead to “more people sharing greater prosperity, health and freedom.”

In his post on Sunday, Wang criticised “lazy thinking” within the AI industry that he said treated superintelligence as inevitable.

“We should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI. We should endeavour ourselves to build a technology which delivers a positive future for humanity, where all humans have greater agency and empowerment,” Wang said.

“I strongly believe this is possible, but likely involves the whole industry taking meaningfully different actions from the “default path” in front of us.”

منبع تصویر، (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images

۹ ماه پس از آغاز جنگ آمریکا و ایران، رسانه‌های آمریکایی در حالی که عملکرد گذشته دولت را زیر سوال می‌برند، با نگرانی به آینده این درگیری نیز می‌نگرند. نشریه آتلانتیک می‌نویسد دولت ترامپ هنوز تصویر روشنی از هزینه‌های مرحله پیشین جنگ به کنگره و افکار عمومی ارائه نکرده و دسترسی به این اطلاعات را محدود کرده است.

همزمان، دونالد ترامپ در گفت‌وگو با فاکس‌نیوز از احتمال آغاز دور تازه‌ای از حملات سخن می‌گوید و تحلیلگران به وال‌استریت جورنال گفته‌اند تهران آمریکا را تضعیف‌شده می‌بیند و محاسبات خود را بر همین اساس تنظیم کرده است.

دولت دونالد ترامپ از پیروزی در جنگ با ایران سخن می‌گوید، اما نشریه آتلانتیک در گزارشی پرسیده است این پیروزی با چه هزینه‌ای به دست آمده و چرا بخش بزرگی از این هزینه هنوز برای افکار عمومی و حتی کنگره آمریکا روشن نیست. محور این گزارش، محدود شدن دسترسی رسانه‌ها و قانونگذاران به اطلاعات مربوط به جنگ است.

به نوشتهٔ این نشریه، پیت هگست، وزیر دفاع آمریکا، در دستورالعملی در ماه مارس، حمایت پنتاگون از سفرهای نظارتی اعضای کنگره به حوزهٔ عملیاتی فرماندهی مرکزی آمریکا (سنتکام) را به موافقت شخص خود مشروط کرده است. آتلانتیک می‌نویسد این محدودیت دامن سناتورهای هر دو حزب را گرفته است. در گزارش آمده که درخواست آن‌ها برای بازدید از پایگاه هوایی العدید در قطر، که در جریان جنگ هدف حملات ایران قرار گرفت، نیز مشمول همین دستورالعمل شده است.

بر اساس این گزارش، برآورد پنتاگون از هزینه عملیات و جایگزینی مهمات مصرف‌شده تا میانه نوامبر به حدود ۴۸ میلیارد دلار رسیده است. آتلانتیک اما تاکید می‌کند که این رقم لزوماً هزینه نهایی نیست و رقم واقعی می‌تواند بسیار بیشتر باشد. دولت ترامپ جداگانه ۶۷ میلیارد دلار بودجه تکمیلی برای هزینه‌های جنگ درخواست کرده است.

فهرست پرسش‌های بی‌پاسخ به پول ختم نمی‌شود. به نوشتهٔ آتلانتیک، میزان خسارت پایگاه‌های آمریکا و شمار دقیق کشته‌ها و مجروحان نظامی هنوز معلوم نیست. گزارش همچنین به حمله به مدرسه‌ شجره طیبه در میناب اشاره می‌کند و می‌نویسد نتیجه تحقیقات سنتکام در این باره هنوز منتشر نشده است.

آتلانتیک نتیجه می‌گیرد که در حالی که ترامپ بار دیگر گزینه حملهٔ نظامی را بررسی می‌کند، شهروندان و قانونگذاران آمریکایی هنوز تصویر روشنی از پیامدهای جنگی که در ماه فوریه آغاز شد و پایانش معلوم نیست ندارند.

همان گزینه‌ای که آتلانتیک از بررسی‌اش خبر داده، در گفت‌وگوی اختصاصی دونالد ترامپ با فاکس‌نیوز صریح‌تر مطرح شده است. رئیس‌جمهوری آمریکا به تری یینگست، خبرنگار ارشد خارجی این شبکه، گفته است اگر توافقی با ایران حاصل نشود، به صدور دستور حملات نظامی پس از آغاز سال نو میلادی تمایل دارد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

ترامپ مذاکره‌کنندگان ایرانی را «رقصنده‌های حرفه‌ای تَپ» توصیف کرده است؛ اصطلاحی در زبان انگلیسی که به افرادی اشاره دارد که با حرف زدن و مانور کلامی، از دادن پاسخ روشن یا اتخاذ تصمیم مشخص طفره می‌روند. او گفته است طرف ایرانی مدام صحبت می‌کند، اما اقدام عملی انجام نمی‌دهد. به گزارش فاکس‌نیوز، ترامپ تهران را به وقت‌کشی متهم کرده و مدعی شده است که رفتار ایران پس از انتخابات آمریکا خصمانه‌تر شده است.

لحن او درباره محاصره دریایی بنادر ایران تندتر بود. فاکس‌نیوز می‌نویسد ترامپ عملا به نیروهای ایرانی هشدار داده که محاصره را به چالش نکشند و گفته است هر شناوری که برای شکستن آن اقدام کند، به سرنوشت دیگر شناورهای نیروی دریایی ایران دچار خواهد شد و به قعر دریا خواهد رفت.

پیش‌بینی او این است که تنش بین دو کشور فعلاً ادامه پیدا می‌کند. تحلیلگرانی که فاکس‌نیوز با آنها صحبت کرده، سامانه‌های موشکی، توان دریایی و شبکه‌های فرماندهی را هدف‌های محتمل مرحلهٔ نخست یک عملیات تازه می‌دانند.

ترامپ در پاسخ به پرسشی درباره اعتراض‌ ضد حکومتی در ایران گفت ویدئوهای منتشرشده را دیده است و از معترضان خواست به اعتراض‌های خود ادامه دهند.

سی‌ان‌ان با بررسی داده‌های دریانوردی گزارش داده که حملات به کشتی‌های تجاری در تنگه هرمز و آب‌های اطراف آن به بالاترین سطح از آغاز جنگ رسیده است. به نوشته این شبکه، در حالی که قیمت نفت رو به کاهش است، تهران می‌کوشد کنترل خود را بر این آبراه دوباره تثبیت کند.

بر اساس این گزارش، شمار حملاتی که در ماه اکتبر به مرکز عملیات تجارت دریایی بریتانیا، نهاد وابسته به نیروی دریایی این کشور، گزارش شده برای نخستین بار از آغاز جنگ در اواخر فوریه از ۳۰ مورد گذشت. تحلیل سی‌ان‌ان از داده‌های این مرکز نشان می‌دهد که در ماه نوامبر نیز تا روز یکشنبه دست‌کم ۲۲ حمله ثبت شده است. میانگین ماهانه پیش از اکتبر حدود ۱۰ مورد بود. این آمار تنگهٔ هرمز، خلیج فارس و دریای عمان را در بر می‌گیرد.

سی‌ان‌ان اما تأکید می‌کند که رقم واقعی احتمالاً بیشتر است. این مرکز فقط مواردی را ثبت می‌کند که از منابع دست اول تأیید شده باشند و خود در گزارش هفتگی‌اش گفته از حوادث دیگری هم خبر دارد که امکان راستی‌آزمایی مستقل آنها نیست. به نوشتهٔ سی‌ان‌ان، گمان می‌رود بسیاری از کشتی‌ها برای شناسایی نشدن دستگاه‌های ردیابی خود را خاموش کرده باشند و این مرکز در ماه اکتبر گفته بود بیشتر کشتی‌های هدف‌گرفته‌شده حاضر به گزارش حمله نیستند.

روایت تهران از این حوادث متفاوت است. به گزارش سی‌ان‌ان، ایران تقریباً هر روز از حادثه‌ای برای کشتی‌های تجاری در حال عبور از تنگه خبر می‌دهد، اما اغلب آنها را به مین‌های دریایی نسبت می‌دهد، نه حمله پهپادی یا موشکی.

سی‌ان‌ان افزایش حملات را به وضعیت اقتصادی ایران ربط می‌دهد. شرکت ردیابی دریایی کپلر در اواخر اکتبر گزارش داده بود که با تخلیه آخرین محموله‌ها در چین، دیگر نفت ایران بیرون از محدودهٔ محاصره آمریکا روی آب نیست و درآمد نفتی این کشور ممکن است تا میانهٔ دسامبر به صفر برسد. کارشناسانی که سی‌ان‌ان به آنها استناد کرده می‌گویند ایران در حال از دست دادن اهرم فشار خود بر این آبراه است و ممکن است برای گرفتن امتیاز از واشنگتن حملات را بیشتر کند.

آژانس بین‌المللی انرژی کاهش اخیر قیمت نفت را ناشی از احیای صادرات کشورهای خلیج فارس می‌داند. به نوشته سی‌ان‌ان، قیمت‌ها پس از اعلام نتایج انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آمریکا هم پایین آمد، چون نگرانی از اقدام نظامی تازهٔ آمریکا فروکش کرد.

اگر ترامپ از موضع قدرت سخن می‌گوید، دو تحلیلگر در وال‌استریت جورنال تصویر دیگری ترسیم کرده‌اند. روئل مارک گرشت و ری تکیه در یادداشتی در بخش دیدگاه‌های این روزنامه استدلال کرده‌اند که رهبران جمهوری اسلامی آمریکا را پس از جنگ ضعیف‌تر می‌بینند و بر همین اساس در حال گذار از وضعیت «نه جنگ، نه صلح» به سیاست «بازدارندگی حداکثری» هستند.

به باور نویسندگان، اگر آمریکا در این رویارویی ناکام بماند، پیامدهای آن به خاورمیانه محدود نخواهد ماند. آنها این سناریو را با پیامدهای راهبردی جنگ کره مقایسه می‌کنند و هشدار می‌دهند که چنین نتیجه‌ای موقعیت واشنگتن را در رقابت با روسیه و چین نیز تضعیف می‌کند.

نویسندگان مقاله اضافه می‌کنند که جمهوری اسلامی در صورت پیروزی ممکن است نفوذ خود را در خلیج فارس گسترش دهد و از موقعیت جغرافیایی‌اش برای فشار اقتصادی و سیاسی بر کشورهای عربی بهره بگیرد. به استدلال آنها، طولانی شدن جنگ و ناتوانی احتمالی واشنگتن در رسیدن به اهدافش می‌تواند این تصور را در مسکو و پکن تقویت کند که آمریکا به دلیل اختلافات داخلی و محدودیت‌های نظامی، توان و ارادهٔ پایبندی به تعهدات راهبردی خود را ندارد.

۹ ماه پس از آغاز جنگ آمریکا و ایران، رسانه‌های آمریکایی در حالی که عملکرد گذشته دولت را زیر سوال می‌برند، با نگرانی به آینده این درگیری نیز می‌نگرند. نشریه آتلانتیک می‌نویسد دولت ترامپ هنوز تصویر روشنی از هزینه‌های مرحله پیشین جنگ به کنگره و افکار عمومی ارائه نکرده و دسترسی به این اطلاعات را محدود کرده است.

نویسندگان مقاله اضافه می‌کنند که جمهوری اسلامی در صورت پیروزی ممکن است نفوذ خود را در خلیج فارس گسترش دهد و از موقعیت جغرافیایی‌اش برای فشار اقتصادی و سیاسی بر کشورهای عربی بهره بگیرد. به استدلال آنها، طولانی شدن جنگ و ناتوانی احتمالی واشنگتن در رسیدن به اهدافش می‌تواند این تصور را در مسکو و پکن تقویت کند که آمریکا به دلیل اختلافات داخلی و محدودیت‌های نظامی، توان و ارادهٔ پایبندی به تعهدات راهبردی خود را ندارد.
